name: curl_options_table
title: Option names, ids, and types from curl_easy_option_next. The filter is a regular expression.

origin.description: You can use curl_options_table() to lookup the type for each option: most options take a string, number, or TRUE/FALSE value, but some options need a special enum/bitmask value.

arguments.name: filter
arguments.text: string: only return options with string in name

origin.details: Option names, ids, and types from curl_easy_option_next. Aliases are omitted. Names are lower case.
origin.value: A data frame with columns name, value, and type.
origin.example:
.libPaths(c(path.expand("~/R/library"), .libPaths()))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(curl))
tbl <- curl_options_table("^url$")
cat(paste(tbl$name, tbl$value, as.character(tbl$type), sep = "=", collapse = "|"))

translation.description: You can use curl_options_table() to lookup the type for each option: most options take a string, number, or TRUE/FALSE value, but some options need a special enum/bitmask value.

arguments.name: filter

translation.details: Option names, ids, and types from curl_easy_option_next. Aliases are omitted. Names are lower case.
translation.value: A list of dicts with keys name, value, and type.
translation.example:
from curl import curl_options_table
rows = curl_options_table("^url$")
print("|".join(f"{row['name']}={row['value']}={row['type']}" for row in rows))
